name: Park Hyatt Shanghai
positioning: Modern-Chinese residence-style hotel on the 79th to 93rd floors of the Shanghai World Financial Centre in Lujiazui
best_for: Travelers who want high-floor views of the Huangpu River or the Shanghai cityscape
Guests who want a Lujiazui base close to the metro

facts.text: The hotel occupies the 79th to the 93rd floors of the Shanghai World Financial Centre.
The hotel is in the heart of the Lujiazui business district.
The hotel is a 5-minute walk from Exit 6 of Lujiazui Metro Station.
Every room has views of either the Huangpu River or the Shanghai cityscape.
Rooms have a separate powder room with a Washlet and a bathroom with a walk-in rain shower and deep soaking tub.
An infinity pool and heated hot tub are on level 85.
The spa offers treatments focused on health, wellbeing and harmonious balance.
Dining Room on level 87 is a contemporary Chinese restaurant serving modern Shanghainese, Zhejiang and Jiangsu cuisines.
100 Century Avenue Steakhouse serves a grill menu of prime beef, market-fresh seafood and premium poultry.
100 Century Avenue Cantonese serves traditional dim sum on the east side of level 91.
100 Century Avenue Bar is on level 91.
The Living Room on level 87 is a residential-style venue that encloses the reception area.

highlights.text: Dining Room was named a Selected Restaurant in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide Shanghai and received One Diamond in the 2026 Black Pearl Restaurant Guide.
The art includes hundreds of ceramics by Liu Jianhua hanging from the ceiling of 100 Century Avenue.
The hotel was designed by New York-based designer Tony Chi as a modern-Chinese residence.
In-house guests can join a complimentary Morning Sound Bowl Floating Experience at Water's Edge on level 85 on Thursdays and Sundays, with reservations required.
Park Salon on level 86 is open exclusively to in-house guests and offers free-flow champagne and premium wines.

considerations.text: Hotel parking spaces are limited and reserved for in-house guests.
The hotel recommends local mapping apps such as Gaode Map or Baidu Map, as international mapping apps may not be accurate in Chinese Mainland.
WhataHotel notes the modern skyscraper setting may lack traditional Shanghai charm.

sources.title: Conde Nast Traveler: Park Hyatt Shanghai
